subject: Fairsun - Marketplace private offer & procurement path
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@fairsun.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer + procurement checklist (FS-4201)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the performance figures looked promising for our recommendation engine tests. Procurement asked me to get a formal mutual action plan (MAP) and a clear billing path for the private offer purchase via AWS Marketplace.

Quick context: we run procurement centrally and need to know whether Redwood can:
- Accept PO to Redwood or via AWS Marketplace private offer?
- Provide monthly invoices and a single invoice for our central finance team?
- Sign a Marketplace Private Offer (POA) + Master Services Agreement (MSA) or do we need a separate SOW?

Can you share a step-by-step procurement timeline (MAP) and any templates (PO template, SOC2 evidence link) so I can feed this to our procurement ops?

Also please include any billing account code/GL guidance — our finance team is strict.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement
Fairsun Analytics
elena@fairsun.com
[attachment: Fairsun_PO_Template.docx]
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer + procurement checklist (FS-4201)

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a draft MAP and a pricing summary that maps the private-offer flow to the billing path you asked about. High level:

- We can accept signing via AWS Marketplace private offer (preferred for licensing + AWS billing) OR we can accept a direct PO to Redwood if procurement requires it.
- For Marketplace private offers: AWS issues the invoice to you, and AWS pays Redwood (Marketplace flow). We can also configure monthly consolidated invoices if needed.
- If you prefer Redwood direct billing, we will invoice monthly to the PO number and can wire/ACH per the payment terms in the offer.

Attached: MAP_Fairsun_Draft_v1.pdf (draft MAP with timeline), pricing_summary_v1.xlsx.

Next steps I recommend: 1) Quick 30-min run-through with procurement + tech to confirm billing account codes, 2) Redwood legal reviews PO template (cc'ing Jordan / Karthik), 3) Execute private offer and sign via DocuSign/AWS as needed.

Proposed near-term timeline in the MAP: sign private offer by 2026-07-23, billing goes live first day of next month after signature.

Would you be available Mon/Tues next week for a short call?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer + procurement checklist (FS-4201)

Hi Elena — quick note from Sales Ops to clarify the billing mechanics and procurement tasks so your team has a checklist: 

1) Marketplace private offer (recommended):
   - Redwood creates private offer in AWS Marketplace tied to deal FS-4201.
   - You accept offer from your AWS account; AWS will generate invoices to Fairsun and remit to Redwood.
   - If you need consolidated monthly invoices, provide the AWS payer account id and purchase order number up front.

2) Direct Redwood invoicing (alternate):
   - Redwood issues monthly invoice to the PO number you provide; payments via ACH/Wire.
   - For vendor setup we supply W-9, vendor form, and Redwood accounting contact.

Procurement checklist (what we need from Fairsun):
- Completed vendor setup form or PO template (you attached one — thanks).
- Company EIN and billing address (for Redwood or AWS depending on route).
- AWS payer account ID if going Marketplace route.
- Desired invoice delivery method (email to ap@fairsun.com or SFTP).

DocuSign link (private offer + MSA): https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?envelopeId=ABC123-FS-4201
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FS-4201

I can prepare the private offer metadata once you confirm the AWS payer account id.

—Karthik

Thanks Karthik — helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal after reviewing your MAP draft: 

- Our preferred flow is AWS Marketplace private offer so AWS handles invoicing to our central finance team.
- We attached our PO template with standard GL and tax language — please have your legal sign off.
- Question on consolidated monthly invoices: can we get invoice line items broken down by product SKUs and monthly usage (token consumption) to push to our chargeback system?

Forwarding our PO template again: [attachment: Fairsun_PO_Template.docx]

On a related note, do you support an implementation milestone (SOW) for the evaluation phase (30-day evaluation plan) that can be referenced in the MAP? Our engineering org wants a short, time-boxed eval with clear acceptance criteria before procurement releases full budget.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — Monica from Finance/Legal here. Thanks for the PO template and the eval request. A few concrete notes and our recommended timeline so procurement has something to commit to: 

- PO review: Redwood legal is fine with your PO with two small redlines (payment net-30 -> net-45 for AWS marketplace routing; standard IP clause clarified). I attached comments in the tracked doc internally.
- SKU-level invoices: yes, Marketplace invoices can include usage detail (we will include token consumption lines). Please share the GL codes you'd like us to map to each SKU.
- Evaluation SOW: we typically run a 30-day evaluation SOW that includes: onboarding checklist, evaluation dataset, acceptance tests (latency, throughput, output-quality spot-checks), and a sign-off form. We can attach the SOW to the MAP and set the evaluation to run immediately after signature.

Proposed procurement MAP timeline (agreed milestones):
- 2026-07-19: Final PO/DocuSign envelope issued to Fairsun
- 2026-07-23: Signed private offer completed and validated in AWS console
- 2026-08-01: Billing live (first invoice covers evaluation month)

I'll start the DocuSign envelope and share the link directly to the signers.

Regards,
Monica Patel
